title: CPF Education Loan Scheme
description: A loan scheme that allows CPF member to use their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay for their own, children’s, spouse’s, siblings' or relatives' government subsidised tuition fees for full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs).
highlights: Allows for the use of OA savings to pay for the government subsidised tuition fees for full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs)
Applications will only be processed after the application period for the approved educational institution has closed
Processing of application generally takes 3 working days upon receipt of the student's enrolment confirmation from the approved educational institution

sections.About this support:
- Allows the use of OA savings to pay for own, children’s, spouse’s, siblings' or relatives' government subsidised tuition fees for [full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-courses-are-covered-by-the-cpf-education-loan-scheme)
- The student (i.e., borrower) would need to start repaying the principal amount withdrawn plus the accrued interest in cash, to the lender’s CPF OA, one year after graduating from or leaving the course of study, whichever occurs earlier

Note:

- OA savings can be used up to the Available Withdrawal Limit under the CPF Education Loan Scheme
- The Available Withdrawal Limit is either 40% of your accumulated OA savings, or your remaining OA balance, whichever is lower
- The amount that can be used is also subject to the tuition fees payable
- If you are 55 or older, you must set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account before using the remaining OA savings, up to the Available Withdrawal Limit.
- You may wish to check how much tuition fees can be paid using [OA savings.](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-much-of-tuition-fees-can-be-paid-using-cpf-ordinary-account-oa-savings)
sections.Who is this for?:
- CPF members/lenders with OA savings are eligible to pay for their own, children’s, spouse’s, or relative’s government subsidised tuition fees using OA savings, up to the Available Withdrawal Limit
- The Available Withdrawal Limit is up to 40% of accumulated OA savings, or the remaining OA balance, whichever is lower
- The CPF member can check the Available Withdrawal Limit through the CPF website using Singpass
- Only full-time diploma / degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs) are covered under this loan scheme
- For the list of approved courses, you may refer to [approved courses under this scheme](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-courses-are-covered-by-the-cpf-education-loan-scheme)
- Here are the alternative education financing options:
  - [MOE Higher Education Student Loan](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-is-the-moe-higher-education-student-loan-hesl)
  - [Other financing options offered by the institutions](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-are-the-financing-options-from-moe-and-the-educational-institutions)
  - [Post-Secondary Education Account funds](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea)
sections.How to apply?:
- Apply online through [“Forms and e-applications"](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications) at [CPF website](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan) with your Singpass
- You must read the accompanying Terms & Conditions, and Procedures & Guidelines before you complete the online form
- Before you submit your application online under the CPF Education Loan Scheme:
  - Check the application period for the approved educational institution you are applying to use CPF savings to pay your tuition fees
  - Ensure you are accepted by the institution and confirm that it is an approved educational institution under the CPF Education Loan Scheme
  - Establish whether you are a new (e.g. fresh intake for AY2024/2025) or existing student (e.g. 2nd year student) under the institution
- You are required to submit 1 (one) application form for each CPF lender, for the entire course of study, unless you enrol into a different AEI
- Please note the application period for use of CPF savings under CPF Education Loan Scheme differs for each AEI
- You may [refer to their schedules here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan/application-schedule)
sections.Where to go:
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only

title: Youth COP
description: Aims to foster positive development and strengthen protective factors, empowering youths as crime-prevention leaders to help their communities thrive, stay safe, and build resilience.

sections.About this support:
Youth COP is a 3-year developmental programme that empowers students to become confident, responsible crime-prevention leaders who help keep their peers and communities safe. In partnership with Neighbourhood Police Centres and selected schools, the programme develops youths into active contributors who serve, protect, and care for their community through meaningful engagement and public education efforts.

Through strong collaboration with families, schools, police, and the wider community, Youth COP equips students with leadership skills, crime-prevention knowledge, and opportunities to make a positive impact. As Crime Prevention Ambassadors, participants build a strong sense of identity and self-worth, gain the competencies to navigate life’s challenges, make informed decisions, and foster safer, more caring school and community environments.
sections.Who is this for?: The programme supports secondary school students in selected schools, with leadership potential by providing guidance, developmental opportunities, and the knowledge and skills to understand laws and their implications. Youth COP nurtures these young people into positive contributors within their schools and communities, grounded in the belief that all youths grow and thrive when supported with strong relationships, meaningful experiences, and opportunities to realise their potential.
sections.How to apply?:
- Students can nominate themselves through the booths in school.
- Students can also be nominated for the programme through school personnel (e.g. teachers).
sections.What to expect?:
- Programme staff will conduct a selection interview with the nominated student (by self or other school referral)  Students will be assessed for their risks, needs and suitability for this programme, within 2 to 3 weeks of referral or sign-up.
- In the event that student is not suitable for the programme, they will be given a letter to explain reasons for rejection and will be directed to other services based on the social worker's recommendations.

title: Epworth Literacy and Behaviour Intervention
description: Offers literacy and behavioural intervention to support children aged 5 to 12 years old with learning difficulties.

sections.About this support:
Offers literacy and behavioural intervention to support children with literacy and behavioural challenges.

Services include:

- Literacy and/or language intervention - provides children between 5 to 12 years old with skills and strategies to overcome their learning challenges and develop literacy skills.
- Behavioural intervention - supports children between 5 to 12 years old in the aspects of essential executive functioning for learning, task readiness, on-seat behaviour, and basic social competency skills.
- Parenting workshops are also offered for parents to increase their knowledge in effective parenting and understanding the needs of their children.
sections.Who is this for?: Children aged between 5 - 12 years old (in pre-schools and mainstream schools) with learning difficulties assessed to be behind their same-aged peers in their literacy and/or language skills.
sections.How to apply?: You may contact the service provider directly for enquiries and to sign up for the programme.
sections.What to expect?: Epworth will screen to assess if the child is eligible and suitable for the programme.

title: Large Families Scheme
description: Provides more support for Singaporean families who have three or more children.
highlights: Increased Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant to $10,000
Large Family MediSave Grant of $5,000
Large Family LifeSG Credits of $1,000 annually, during the years that the third and subsequent child turns 1 to 6 years old

sections.About this support:
The SG Child Support Package announced at the 2026 National Day Rally will replace the Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. The increased CDA First Step Grant for large families will cease from April 2027. As Child Credits will be given to all eligible children under the Package, Large Family LifeSG Credits will also cease, with no disbursements in 2027. More details on additional support for large families will be provided at a later date.

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

Families will receive additional support of up to $16,000 for each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child, on top of existing Baby Bonus Scheme benefits.

**Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant**

- $10,000 CDA First Step Grant (increase from $5,000)
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025
- Deposited into the eligible child's CDA within two weeks of CDA opening
- Can be used to defray approved preschool and healthcare expenses of the child and/or his/her siblings

**Large Family MediSave Grant**

- $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025
- Deposited into the mother's MediSave account, following child's Baby Bonus enrolment
- Can be used to offset the mother’s pregnancy and delivery costs, or approved dependant's healthcare expenses

**Large Family LifeSG Credits**

- $1,000 annually in Large Family LifeSG Credits
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child, including those turning 1 to 6 years old in 2025
- Credits are disbursed to the CDA trustee of the child and accessible via LifeSG mobile app
- Can be used at any merchant that accepts payments using PayNow UEN QR or NETS QR, to defray household expenses
- Credits are valid for 12 months from disbursement, with the expiry date displayed in the LifeSG mobile app
sections.Who is this for?:
Families with a third or subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025 will receive:

- the increased CDA First Step Grant of $10,000,
- a $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant, and
- $1,000 annually in Large Family LifeSG Credits during the years that the child turns 1 to 6 years old*.

*The Large Family LifeSG Credits also applies to existing large families with at least one child aged six or below.
sections.How to apply?: No application is required.
sections.Phone number: Baby Bonus and Large Families Scheme hotline: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222)

description: One-off $400 top-up to Child Development Account (CDA) for Singapore Citizens aged 0 to 6 from September 2023.
highlights: One-off $400 top-up to Child Development Account (CDA) for Singapore Citizens aged 0 to 6 in 2023
Top-up will be credited from September 2023
Eligible child must open a CDA by 30 June 2024

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

- Children born on 1 Jan 2017 who have started primary school in 2023 will receive the Edusave top-up instead.
- Eligible child must open a CDA by 30 June 2024.

title: Child Development Account
description: Special savings account for the child, which can be used for approved areas of child-raising expenditure, including healthcare and preschool fees.
highlights: CDA First Step Grant enhanced by $2,000 for eligible Singaporean children
Up to $15,000 in Government co-matching  for eligible Singaporean children
Enhancements will apply to eligible Singaporean children born on or after 14 February 2023

sections.About this support:
The SG Child Support Package announced at the 2026 National Day Rally will replace the current Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. Those currently on the Baby Bonus Scheme will be automatically transitioned to the Package. In the meantime, existing payouts will continue as usual. 

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

The Child Development Account (CDA) is a special savings account for the child, which can be used for defray child-raising costs. The First Step Grant is automatically deposited after the CDA is opened, and subsequent savings will be co-matched by the Government, up to a cap.

Eligible Singaporean children born on or after 14 Feb 2023 will qualify for the following enhanced CDA benefits announced at Budget 2023.

**Child Development Account First Step Grant:**

- $5,000 automatically credited into the CDA upon account opening.

**Government co-matching of CDA savings:**

- Eligible Singaporean children are entitled to Government co-matching up to a cap of $4,000 for the first child, $7,000 for the second child, $9,000 for the third and fourth child, and $15,000 for the fifth child and beyond.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Child is a Singapore Citizen
- Children born on or after 14 Feb 2023
- Parents are lawfully married
- Children of unwed parents may be eligible for CDA benefits if they are born on or after 1 September 2016.
sections.How to apply?:
All parents can apply for Baby Bonus Scheme at LifeSG:

- [Bundled service](https://www.life.gov.sg/services/birth-registration) together with child’s birth registration
- [Direct application](https://www.life.gov.sg/services/baby-bonus) for child who has already registered for birth
sections.Email / Form: [Submit an enquiry through Ask Baby Bonus](https://ask.gov.sg/msf/questions/new?topic=MSF Baby Bonus)
sections.Phone number:
MSF Consolidated Hotline: 1800 111 2222

(say ‘Baby Bonus’ when asked for the hotline you want to reach)

Operating hours: Mon to Fri 8.30am to 6pm | Saturday: 8.30am to 1pm

(Closed on Public Holidays)

Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines

title: Life! Mentors
description: A 5-8 year mentoring programme that supports children (6-13 years old) a fair chance to succeed in life.

sections.About this support:
The programme core services includes

- 1-1 mentoring
- Group mentoring
- Family bonding activities
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore citizens/ Singapore PRs aged 6 – 13 years old from vulnerable backgrounds (e.g. ComLink+ families, parental incarceration, referral from school counsellors).
sections.How to apply?: Walk in to any of  Life Community Services Society centres or referral by school counsellors or fill in the online contact form (https://life-community.org/contact-us/)
sections.What to expect?: Programme staff will conduct intake and needs assessment within one month of the referral. For higher needs and urgent cases, it will be conducted within two weeks. Programme staff will contact the caregiver via phone call or text messages to introduce the programme, share the online intake form, and arrange a home visit.

title: SHINE Children and Youth Services - Learning and Social Support Programme
description: Provides literacy and language intervention to children aged between 7 and 12 years old (in mainstream schools) with learning difficulties.

sections.About this support:
Provides literacy and language intervention to children aged 7 to 12 years (in mainstream schools) with learning difficulties.

Services include:
* Actualise Learning Potential and Promote Skills (ALPS) Language and literacy intervention programme - addresses the learning needs of children between 7 to 12 years old who typically lag 2 to 3 years behind their same-aged peers in language or literacy levels.
* Parenting sessions to equip and empower parents and caregivers to understand the needs of their children and better engage with them.
* Reading Odyssey - enhances the reading ability of children between 7 to 12 years old and to improve their motivation to read.
sections.Who is this for?: Children aged 7 to 12 years (in mainstream schools) with learning difficulties.
sections.How to apply?: You may contact the service provider directly for enquiries and to sign up for the programme.
sections.What to expect?: The centre will conduct an intake assessment and consultation session with the child to better understand their needs and discuss follow up support and suitability for the programme.

title: The Builders Project
description: Aims to increase social capital and social discipline, and accomplish positive outcomes in Primary 4-6 school children who have been assessed to have higher needs.

sections.About this support: The Builders Project is an early intervention programme targeting Primary 4-5 school children that aims to promote positive school climate and culture that are conducive for achieving social capital and social discipline. The programme works with the parents and teachers of the identified students which leads to better school outcomes such as lower chronic school absenteeism, premature withdrawal from school and other adolescent risk behaviours.
sections.Who is this for?:
P4 to P6 children who:

- Are in mainstream primary schools
- Have been assessed to have higher need
sections.How to apply?: - Schools will refer students to the programme.
sections.What to expect?:
- The one year programme is available in selected partner schools.
- Lutheran Community Care Services (LCCS) will administer a pre-screening tool to students referred by teachers and social workers.
- Based on the results, LCCS and teachers will jointly decide on the identified students who are suitable for further support.

title: MightyKids, Families & Community (MightyKFC)
description: MightyKFC is a developmental mentoring programme that aims to nurture at-risk children and youth in the Telok Blangah region.

sections.About this support:
MightyKFC is a developmental mentoring programme with the following service components:

- Centre based activities
- Life skills workshops
- Individual mentoring
- Community service
- Parent-child bonding session
sections.Who is this for?:
- MightyKFC’s client group is latchkey children and youth from the lower income group, aged 4 – 16 years old.
- MightyKFC targets children and youth who primarily reside or study in schools in the Telok Blangah region.
sections.How to apply?:
You may:

- Walk into the centre
- Email to [mkfc@life-community.org](mailto:mkfc@life-community.org)
- Call the centre at [62707198](tel:62707198)
sections.What to expect?:
- An intake interview will be arranged to register for the programme.
- Upon successful registration, services will be provided to the service users for the duration of the programme at the activity centre.

title: Halogen SPARK!
description: A structured evidence-based entrepreneurship curriculum that targets Secondary 3 students who are from the G1/G2 Subject Based Banding (SBB) Stream that improves better school-focused outcomes, including their attendance and academic performance.

sections.About this support:
Halogen SPARK! is an upstream intervention programme that targets Secondary students who are from the G1/G2 SBB stream. It targets pre/low/mid-risk students from the Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) and/or come from challenging and disadvantaged backgrounds.

The programme is a structured evidence-based programme developed by NFTE (Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship), where the key objectives are to increase service users' social-emotional and academic competencies through the incorporation of English and Math in the programme curriculum. It supports the development of numeracy and literacy skills through the entrepreneurship modules, and aims to instill self-confidence and self-efficacy in youths.
sections.Who is this for?: Secondary 3 students who are from the G1/G2 Subject Based Banding (SBB) stream
sections.How to apply?:
- Schools will refer the students to the programme at the start of the calendar year.
- Halogen SPARK! and teachers will jointly decide on the identified students on their service eligibility.
sections.What to expect?:
- The one year programme is available in selected partner schools.
- Halogen SPARK! will conduct a pre-programme survey for all enrolled students for the purpose of further adjustments to the programmes depending on the student demographics.

title: The Scaffold Programme
description: Supports Secondary 1 and 2 students, who have been identified to have higher needs, including socio-emotional and behavioural difficulties, at risk of delinquency, and observed to have low school connectedness.

sections.About this support:
The Scaffold Programme (TSP) is an upstream, early intervention programme that supports lower secondary school students in mainstream schools, who are predisposed to latent risk factors or premature withdrawal from school.

TSP aims to provide quality school social work intervention for students and their ecosystems that lead to improved school outcomes, reduced referrals to downstream programmes, improvement in parent-child relationships and school-student attachment.
sections.Who is this for?:
Secondary 1 and 2 students who have been identified to have higher needs including:

- Socio-emotional and behavioural difficulties
- At risk of delinquency
- Observed to have low school connectedness
sections.How to apply?: The programme adopts a class-based design – i.e. school teachers will identify and refer suitable classes to join the programme at the start of the calendar year.
sections.What to expect?:
- The one year programme is available in selected partner schools
- Agency will have a discussion with relevant school personnel on the needs of the classes
- The agency will then customise the service component to address the unique needs of the class

title: Our Lives Our Voices (OLOV)
description: OLOV aims to empower clients to become self-advocates and foster an inclusive society where PWIDs can independently participate in the community in a meaningful manner. Through personalised training and peer support, it builds confidence and independence.

sections.About this support: The programme provides structured, personalised training supported by a customised web application, peer-led facilitation, and community engagement. It equips PWIDs with essential communication and interpersonal skills, empowering them to discover their strengths, express their views, take on meaningful community roles, and pursue greater autonomy, purpose, and active participation in society.
sections.Who is this for?:
1. PWIDs aged 18 years and above with an IQ below 70
2. PWIDs who demonstrate ability to participate in group training sessions, express basic intentions and preferences.
3. PWIDs registered under MINDS programmes
sections.How to apply?:
Interested applicants can apply through the following:

1. Email to [olov@minds.org.sg](mailto:olov@minds.org.sg)

2.  Submit the form via https://tinyurl.com/olovinterest

3. Call 65478503
sections.What to expect?:
1. Basic screening will be conducted to ensure that PWIDs meet the criteria
2. PWIDs will also be assessed over 2 trial sessions to determine suitability and interest.
3. Enrollment is throughout the year.

title: Youth GO! Programme
description: An engagement and intervention programme for youths who may benefit from additional support (aged 12-21) that helps them stay focused in their studies/work, remain crime-free, develop problem-solving skills and be resilient.

sections.About this support:
- Youth GO! is an engagement and intervention programme that supports youths who may benefit from additional support.
- Its objectives are to help youths who may benefit from additional support be meaningfully engaged in their studies or work, stay crime-free, develop problem-solving skills and be resilient individuals.
sections.Who is this for?:
Youths who:

- are Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents (PR)
- are between 12 - 21 years old
- Diplay the following:
  - Pro-criminal attitude/behaviour;
  - Physically/verbally aggressive behaviour; and/or
  - Subject to negative peer influence

Youths who had completed the Guidance Programme (GP), Streetwise Programme (SWP), Youth Enhanced Supervision (YES) and/probation but require further support, and youths who are out-of-school and not engaged in meaningful work, can be eligible for the YGP, subject to meeting the above criteria.
sections.How to apply?:
- Referrals can be made by contacting the respective Youth GO! service provider according to the region of the youth's residential address or the hotspot area.
- Please refer to [Youth GO! Programme webpage](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/help-those-in-need/article/programmes/Youth-GO-Programme) for information on the regions served by the different service providers, and their contact information.
sections.What to expect?:
- For hotspot referrals, Youth GO! workers will work towards befriending the youth to assess if they fit the criteria of the target clientele.
- Where referrals are successful, Youth GO! workers will continue to engage the youth and conduct casework and intervention through positive engagement activities and case counselling sessions.

title: Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA)
description: Provides educational financial support for eligible Singapore Citizens' post-secondary education.
highlights: Funds can be used for approved programmes, repay government loans, and financial schemes
No application needed

sections.About this support:
- PSEA Funds can be used to pay:
  - one's own or siblings’ approved education programmes at approved institutions
  - government education loans and financial schemes
- PSEA balances earn interest at the same rate as the CPF Ordinary Account (CPF-OA), currently 2.5% per annum
- Unused PSEA funds will be transferred to the CPF-OA when the account holder turns 31, subject to CPF-OA usage rules
sections.Who is this for?:
- You must be a Singapore Citizen with a balance in either:
  - the Child Development Account (CDA) when it is closed
  - the Edusave Account when turning 17 years old or is no longer studying in a Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded school, whichever is later
- The PSEA will also be opened for Singapore Citizens who are:
  - eligible for PSEA top-ups by the Government
  - recipient of the first payment of the National Service Housing, Medical and Education (NS HOME) Awards
  - recipient of the annual education bursary under the Home Ownership Plus Education (HOPE) Scheme
sections.How to apply?: No application required.
sections.Where to go:
[MOE Customer Service Centre, 1 North Buona Vista Drive MOE Building, Podium Block Singapore 138675](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=138675)

Note: By appointment only.

title: CARENIGHTS
description: Supports children aged 6 to 14 from vulnerable families with structured evening care services.

sections.About this support: The CareNights programme is a structured evening care for children aged 6 to 14 from vulnerable families, including those referred through ComLink+ or other community partners. It addresses a critical gap in after-school support, particularly helping caregivers who are working, attending training, or managing caregiving responsibilities.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Caregivers with children aged 6 to 14 and are experiencing caregiving challenges
- Low income (gross household income not exceeding $4,500 per month or per capita income not exceeding $1,125 per month) and/or ComLink+ families
- Families coping with extenuating circumstances beyond those described above will be admitted on a case-by-case basis
sections.How to apply?:
- Referral through schools, social service agencies, and government agencies
- Submission of enquiries through Morning Star Community Services' Website
sections.What to expect?:
- Structured evening care
- The agency provide safe and nuturing environment during evening hours.
- The agency aims to strengthen parent-child through facilited bonding activities and workshops.

title: Care Corner Learning and Special Needs Support Programme
description: Provides literacy, language, and numeracy intervention to children aged between 5 and 13 years old (in mainstream schools) with learning difficulties.

sections.About this support:
The programme provides learning support to children in mainstream schools struggling with learning difficulties such as:

- Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
- Autism Spectrum Disorder (ADD)
- Central Auditory Processing Disorder
- Developmental Delay
- Dyslexia
- Dyscalculia
- Dysgraphia
- Dyspraxia
- Specific Language Impairment
- Sensory Processing Disorder

Services includes:

- KidsReady (N2 to K2) - For children attending preschool / development supporting-learning support (DS-LS) programme who need more support in English, Mathematics, handwriting and fine motor skills
- KidsLearn (P1 to P6) - For primary school children needing learning support in English & Mathematics.
sections.Who is this for?: Children aged 4 to 13 in mainstream schools struggling with learning difficulties
sections.How to apply?: You may contact the service provider directly for enquiries or complete the online referral form: https://form.jotform.com/CC_LSN/lsnreferral
sections.What to expect?: Care Corner will conduct a pre-intake assessment to screen if the child is suitable for the programme.

title: Babes Pregnancy Crisis Support
description: For individuals aged 21 and below needing support with their pregnancy, so that they are aware of their options and are able to make an informed decision regarding their pregnancy.

sections.About this support:
Babes supports pregnant teens through:

- Casework and counselling
- 24-hour helpline
- Practical support (befriender, baby essentials, employment & back to school assistance etc)
- Information & resources
- Outreach and youth engagement events
sections.Who is this for?:
- Pregnant teenager who needs help; Anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
sections.How to apply?: If you are a pregnant teen who needs help, know of one who needs help or need information about teenage pregnancy, please contact Babes' 24-hour helpline at 6206 6641 or text via WhatsApp at 8111 3535 to speak to the caseworkers.
sections.What to expect?:
- Teenagers who require help with their pregnancy and/or anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy may contact Babes via the 24-hour helpline (call/text).
- When an enquiry is attended to, the Helpliner will also assess if the teenager is eligible to be a case under Babes. Should the assessment be one that Babes can assist, Babes will arrange for a meeting with the teenager and/or her family/partner within 3-5 working days to assess the needs and provide the necessary support and guidance.

title: MUIS Zakat Financial Assistance
description: Provides monthly financial assistance and support in other forms to eligible low-income Muslim households.
highlights: Monthly financial assistance for eligible individuals
Support for emergency needs and burial expenses
Study grants and food vouchers available
Assessment based on Per Capita Income of $500 or lower for eligibility

sections.About this support:
Potential benefits include:

- Monthly financial support: Dependent on Per Capita Income (PCI) criteria
- Settlement of debt: One-time settlement of arrears for basic necessities (utility and conservancy charges)
- Emergency assistance: Renders emergency assistance in times of crisis such as natural disasters, fire, or accidents
- Burial expenses: Covers burial expenses incurred upon death of a Zakat beneficiary and their immediate family members
- Study grants: Subsidies for national examinations mosque-based part-time Islamic education, and low-income students with special needs
- Fidyah food vouchers: To purchase food supplies at approved Fidyah retailers islandwide
sections.Who is this for?:
- Available to Muslim Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Per Capita Income (PCI) must be $500 or lower to qualify
- Applicants will undergo an assessment interview with a Social Development Officer (SDO) at the nearest Social Development (SD) mosque
- Required documents: NRIC, birth certificate, income and bank documents, and other relevant supporting documents
- Outcome notified by mail within up to 6 weeks
sections.How to apply?:
- Call a Social Development (SD) mosque closest to your home for an appointment.
- Schedule an assessment interview with an SDO.
- During the interview, please prepare to bring your personal identification documents, such as NRIC and birth certificate, income and bank documents (payslips, CPF statements, bank books etc.), and other relevant supporting documents (bills, medical memos, referral letters etc.) to help verify your application

title: SkillsFuture Credit
description: For Singapore Citizens aged 25 and above to pay for or offset the out-of-pocket course fees of approved courses.
highlights: SkillsFuture Credits can be used on top of existing SWDA course fee subsidies

title: MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) Scheme
description: Loan scheme to help students who are taking MOE-subsidised diploma, undergraduate or postgraduate programmes in publicly-funded post-secondary education institutions to finance their tuition fees and borrow a living allowance loan for other education-related expenses. It also helps undergraduates to finance cost of institution-approved overseas student programme.
highlights: Base provision and means-tested balance fee coverage components under the HESL scheme can cover up to 100% of subsidised tuition fees for eligible Singapore Citizen (SC) students
Eligible students who meet the income eligibility criteria can also apply for a living allowance loan component under the HESL scheme to cover their education expenses
Loan is interest-free during the course of study; interest and repayment commence upon a student’s graduation or leaving the institution

sections.About this support:
For Diploma students
There are two loan components under HESL:
(i)     Base provision to cover up to 90% of subsidised tuition fees payable, depending on the student’s citizenship;
(ii)   Means-tested provisions
·  Loan to cover remaining 10% of subsidised tuition fees (for SC only)
·  Living allowance loan of up to $3,200 per academic year
For Undergraduate and Postgraduate students
There are two loan components under HESL:
(i)     Base provision to cover up to 90% of subsidised tuition fees payable, depending on the student’s citizenship;
(ii)   Means-tested provisions
· Loan to cover remaining 10% of subsidised tuition fees (for SC undergraduates only)
· Living allowance loan of up to $4,100 per academic year (for full-time undergraduate students only)
· Loan to cover up to $12,000 for the cost of one institution-approved overseas student programme (for full-time SC undergraduates only)
sections.Who is this for?:
The HESL will be available to the following students, and the loan components available will depend on the student’s citizenship and level of study:

- SC, Singapore Permanent Resident (PR) and international student (IS) studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma courses in any of the local polytechnics.
- SC and PR studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma courses in Institute of Technical Education (ITE).
- SC and PR studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma and undergraduate programmes in LASALLE College of the Arts (LASALLE), Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) and University of the Arts Singapore (UAS).
- SC, PR and IS studying full-time MOE-subsidised undergraduate, full-time MOE-subsidised postgraduate by coursework, and full-time/part-time MOE-subsidised postgraduate by research programmes in autonomous universities.
- SC studying part-time MOE-subsidised undergraduate programmes in autonomous universities.

Depending on the level of study and type of institution, the means-tested loan provisions are for:

- SC and PR with gross monthly household per capita income (PCI)^ of $3,500 or less.
- IS with gross monthly household PCI of $1,875 or less.

^Monthly PCI is computed based on total monthly gross household income (GHI) divided by number of family members living in the same household.
sections.How to apply?:
- The following students can apply for HESL via the new [StudentLoanSG (SLSG)](https://go.gov.sg/slsg) portal from July 2026.
  - Newly matriculated students in Academic Year (AY) 2026 intake; and
  - Existing students (before AY2026 intake) who do not have Tuition Fee Loan (TFL) and Study Loan (SL) for their current course of study.
- Refer to the respective institution website for details on application window period and application procedures.
- Existing students who have already taken up TFL and/or SL will continue to receive their current loan provision.  No action is required from them.  However, if they wish to apply for new or additional loan provision under the HESL scheme, they should first approach their institution for advice and assessment of needs.

sections.Who is this for?:
- Child is a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident (at least one immediate family member in the same household must be a Singapore Citizen)
- Both you and your spouse are each working at least 56 hours a month
- Child must attend a Student Care Centre registered with MSF
- For children attending SCCs aged 7 to 14 years old (Primary 1 to Secondary 2) in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the monthly gross household income must be $4,500 or less for families with 4 or fewer members, or monthly household income per capita must be $1,125 or less for families with 5 or more members.   For children attending SSCCs aged 7 to 18 years old in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the monthly gross household income must be $9,200 or less for families with 4 or fewer members, or monthly household income per capita must be $2,300 or less for families with 5 more members. **How Income is Calculated**

- For salaried employees:
Based on average gross monthly income over 12 months from CPF records or the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 years).
Includes: basic salary, bonuses, commissions, overtime pay, allowances, cash rewards, and employee CPF contributions.
- For self-employed individuals:
Based on average trade income over 12 months from the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 years), or income declared to CPF Board.

**Note:** Family members refer to the child’s grandparents or siblings below 21 years old who live at the same address, are not working or have no income, and are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

Your gross monthly income will be determined via HOMES as part of the means-test.

For further information, please refer to [MSF | Student Care Fee Assistance](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/student-care/for-parents/student-care-fee-assistance).

description: EIPIC is a centre-based programme that provides therapy and educational intervention for children aged 0-6 years who require medium to high levels of early intervention (EI) support.

sections.About this support:
EIPIC is a centre-based programme that provides therapy and educational intervention for children aged 0 to 6 years who require medium to high levels of early intervention (EI) support.

The continuum of EI services include:

- EIPIC Under-2s
  - Targeted at children under 2 years old
  - Trains parents/caregivers so that they can effectively carry out intervention strategies in the child’s daily routines at home
- EIPIC@Centre
  - Provides both therapy and educational intervention services, typically in small groups
- DS-Plus
  - Provided in preschools targeted at children aged 2 to 6 years requiring low levels of EI support, and are attending preschools.
sections.Who is this for?:
Children who are:

- From birth to 6 years old
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents;
- Assessed by a paediatrician to be at risk of a developmental, intellectual, sensory or physical disability, or a combination of disabilities; and
- Not concurrently enrolled in any other ECDA-funded EI programmes (i.e. DS-LS, DS-Plus programmes).
sections.How to apply?:
- You may approach a doctor at any polyclinic to obtain referral for assessment at the Department of Child Development (DCD) at KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) or Child Development Unit (CDU) at National University Hospital (NUH).
- Alternatively, you may approach a private paediatrician for assessment and recommendation for EIPIC.
- If your child is assessed to be suitable for EIPIC, the hospital or the private paediatrician will recommend EIPIC and submit the application to SG Enable upon your consent.

More information can be found on the [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/therapy-intervention/early-intervention-programme-for-infants-children).
sections.What to expect?:
- Upon receiving the referral, SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days to provide necessary information to help you make an informed decision on your choice of EI Centre.
- Your selected EI Centre will contact you within 2 weeks of referral to arrange an interview and assessment of your child.
- Enrolment into a suitable programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies at the centre and approval of the respective centre management.

title: MyCareersFuture
description: The one-stop portal for job search and application needs. It uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to help jobseekers discover career opportunities, make career transitions, or search for jobs based on skills matches.  It also provides valuable career-related resources, including career insights and career guidance to facilitate their career planning and career development processes.
highlights: Our latest Job-to-Skills job matching algorithm connects you with opportunities tailored to your skills and experience.
Utilise CareersFinder to discover personalised upskilling and career recommendations based on your unique profile.
Filter jobs eligible for Government support such as Career Conversion Programmes, Graduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme and Mid-Career Pathways Programmes
Elevate your skills with our curated articles, webinars, and courses designed for your professional growth.

sections.About this support:
- **Advanced Matching Algorithm: **Our latest Job-to-Skills job matching algorithm connects you with opportunities tailored to your skills and experience.
- **CareersFinder by MyCareersFuture: **[CareersFinder](https://careersfinder.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/) harnesses Government data and artificial intelligence to help individuals discover personalised upskilling and career recommendations based on their unique profile to achieve their career goals.
- **Government Support Eligibility: **Filter jobs eligible for Government support such as:
  - Career Conversion Programmes (CCP) if you are open to reskill and change career/occupations
  - GRaduate Industry and Traineeship Programme (GRIT) if you are a fresh graduate looking for a traineeship opportunity, and
  - Mid-Career Pathways Programmes (MCPP) if you are a mature individual looking for a mid-career attachments.
- **CareersCompass by MyCareersFuture:** Access curated articles, career guides and expert insights to help you navigate career planning, skills development and job search strategies.
- **CareersHorizon by MyCareersFuture: **A one-stop digital platform for career-related event registrations and management. It enables Singaporeans to access a comprehensive suite of career resources, including online articles, virtual career events, seminars, and workshops. The platform also offers micro-learning content, such as podcasts, covering topics relevant to all career stages. Additionally, it supports Singaporeans in searching and registering for career events, and it also facilitates networking opportunities between employers and individuals.
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are looking to plan their careers, make career transitions, or search for jobs.
sections.How to apply?: Embark on your journey to professional success with [MyCareersFuture](https://www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/).

title: The GRIT Academy
description: Mentoring programme for youths-at-risk in Jurong.

sections.About this support: The GRIT Academy (TGA) aims to provide individual mentoring support for youths-at-risk aged between 11 to 17 years old residing or studying in schools in Jurong; and serve as the primary relationship holder to follow through with the youths as they transit to other youth programmes.
sections.Who is this for?:
The target clientele is youths-at-risk aged between 11 to 17 years old residing or studying in schools in Jurong (i.e. Jurong West, Jurong East and Taman Jurong).

Applicants must fulfil at least one of the following criteria to be eligible for the programme:

1. Youths who lack meaningful engagements such as those not attending Co-Curricular Activities, as well as youths who often loiter at public areas such as playgrounds and void decks.
2. Youths with underprivileged background such as youths from low-income families, students receiving the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme and youths staying in rental flats.
3. Youths exhibiting at-risk behaviour such as poor affiliation to schools, minor behavioural issues, socio-emotional issues and/or peer issues.
sections.How to apply?: Complete the form on https://lakeside.org.sg/our-services/the-grit-project/ and email it to [thegritproject@lakeside.org.sg](mailto:thegritproject@lakeside.org.sg).
sections.What to expect?: Screening for potential service users will take approximately 2 weeks from the referral/youth sign-up. Adjustment to the screening time frame will be considered based on the assessed urgency.

title: Infant and Childcare Subsidies
description: Provides tiered subsidies to help cover infant care and childcare fees for Singapore Citizen children from different income backgrounds.
highlights: Working applicants: Basic Subsidy of $600 for infant care and $300 for childcare
Non-working applicants: Basic Subsidy of $150 for infant care and childcare
Additional Subsidy for working applicants

sections.About this support:
**Working applicants (mother or single father who works at least 56 hours per month)**

- Basic Subsidy of $600 for infant care and $300 for childcare
- Additional Subsidy of up to $710 for infant care and up to $467 for childcare

**Non-working applicants**

- Basic Subsidy of $150 for infant care and childcare
- Eligible applicants who are not working or who are non-parent caregivers can apply for Special Approval to receive the higher Basic Subsidy and Additional Subsidy that working applicants receive
sections.Who is this for?:
Types of subsidies
Eligibility criteria
For all subsidies
- Child must be a Singapore Citizen
- Enrolled in an infant care or childcare centre licensed by ECDA
Additional Subsidy
- Working applicants (mother or single father who works at least 56 hours per month)
- Monthly household income of up to $12,000, or monthly household income per capita of up to $3,000 for larger families with 5 or more family members in the same household
  - From 1 January 2027, monthly household income thresholds will be raised to $15,000, or $3,400 per capita
Special Approval
- Main subsidy applicants who are not working due to the following reasons:
  - Looking for a job
  - Studying, training, or on course for at least 56 hours a month
  - Pregnancy
  - Medically unfit for work due to hospitalisation, long-term illness and/or permanent disability
  - Taking care of a special needs child
  - Taking care of a sick family member who requires a full-time caregiver
  - Caring full-time for a younger child aged 24 months and below who is not enrolled in a preschool
  - Incarcerated
  - Non-parent caregivers who are caring for the child such as grandparents, legal guardian, foster parents, and head of a children’s home
- Families who are tenants of a rental flat under the HDB’s Public Rental Scheme or are beneficiaries of ComCare Short-To-Medium-Term Assistance (SMTA) or Long-Term-Assistance (LTA) will automatically qualify for maximum preschool subsidies upon application for Special Approval
sections.How to apply?: Refer to Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) [website](https://www.ecda.gov.sg/parents/preschool-subsidies/how-to-apply-or-make-changes-to-subsidies) to apply or make changes to subsidies
